correctness.rationale: For a nonzero rank-one map R=a⊗f, the Rota–Baxter equation forces a²=λa and simultaneously f∘L_a=μf, f∘R_a=νf, μ+ν=λ. The semigroup product is ab=rho(a)gamma(b)^T. This yields exactly the three square-zero marginal types and a fourth nonzero quasi-idempotent type. The row/column map has fiber dimension d=(m-1)(n-1), while commuting scaled projection images have ranks n,m with rank-one overlap. Counting compatible nonzero functionals in each disjoint case and dividing by q-1 reconstructs the formula. Direct multiplication-table enumeration reproduced all seven finite examples, including nonprime F4; enumeration is explicitly not a general proof.

originality.rationale: The full original Guo–Rosenkranz–Zheng classification covers semigroups with at most three elements, whereas a genuinely two-sided rectangular band has at least four. Its universal coefficient test is not a rank-one enumerative formula. Jian constructs left-multiplier operators from quasi-idempotents; Gubarev counts nonzero-weight operators on direct sums of fields; Benito–Gubarev–Pozhidaev analyze quadratic/simple algebras. Exact comparison against current accessible prior claims on full matrices, truncated polynomial rings, radical-square-zero quiver algebras and triangular matrix algebras gives different algebra products, and none implies this two-parameter rectangular-band census. Relevant semantic record searches returned other settings, not a stronger covering claim. No negative search is treated as a proof of global priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier rank-one classifications of general Munn/sandwich algebras could imply the formula indirectly.
The present self-review is not an independent publication-priority audit.

value.rationale: Rectangular bands are canonical finite completely simple semigroups with two independently varying size parameters, and semigroup-algebra Rota–Baxter classifications had motivated extensions beyond small orders. The complete rank-one census gives a natural exactly computable invariant for every m,n and finite field, distinguishes square-zero from quasi-idempotent image mechanisms, and exhibits a nonzero annihilator allowing R²=R for m,n>=2, unlike the full-matrix setting. It is not a mere arbitrary finite slice or a reformulation of known rank-one counts in a different algebra.
